stanzas: Sing, tongue, the mystery of the glorious
which, as the ransom of the world,
the fruit of a noble womb,
the king of the nations, poured out.
Given to us, born for us
and having lived in the world,
the seed of the word sown,
the days of his dwelling here
he closed in a wondrous order.
On the night of the last supper,
in the foods the law prescribed,
as food to the band of twelve
he gives himself with his own hands.
The Word made flesh makes true bread
and the wine becomes the blood of Christ;
to make firm a sincere heart
let us venerate with bowed heads,
give way to the new rite;
let faith supply what is lacking
To the Begetter and the Begotten
to the one proceeding from both

notes: line 1.4: 'pretium' is 'price', the price paid for the world.
line 1.5-6: 'fructus ventris generosi' stands beside 'rex gentium': the king of the nations, the fruit of a noble womb, poured out the blood.
line 4.1-2: 'Verbum caro' may be read as one phrase, 'the Word made flesh', or 'Word, flesh' in apposition; the line plays on verbum (word) and caro (flesh).
line 5.3: 'documentum' is 'teaching, example', here the rites of the old law.
line 6.5: 'the one proceeding from both' is the Holy Spirit.
